title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 75
paragraphs: When the Lacedaemonians learned what Cleomenes was up to, they grew afraid and proceeded to bring him back to Sparta to rule on the same terms as before. But no sooner had he returned than a madness seized him — he had never been entirely of sound mind — and whenever he met one of the Spartans on the street he would strike him in the face with his staff. As he kept doing this and had plainly lost his reason, his kinsmen bound him in stocks. While he was so bound, he noticed that his guard had been left alone by the others, and he asked him for a knife. At first the guard, a Helot, would not give it, but Cleomenes threatened him with what he would do afterwards if he refused, and at last the man was intimidated into handing it over. Then Cleomenes, once he had the blade, began to mutilate himself from the legs upward, slicing his flesh lengthways up from the legs to the thighs, from the thighs to the loins and flanks, until at last he reached his belly; cutting this into strips he died. Most of the Greeks say that this happened to him because he bribed the Pythian prophetess to give the answer she did about Demaratus. The Athenians alone say it was because, when he invaded Eleusis, he laid waste the sacred precinct of the Two Goddesses. The Argives say it was because he dragged out from their sanctuary of Argos those of their people who had fled there for refuge after the battle, slew them, and even set fire to the grove itself, thinking it of no account.
